slice: South-west working-class districts — DISTRICT 8 (canals: Kênh Tàu Hủ / Kênh Đôi / Rạch Ông / Chánh Hưng), BÌNH TÂN, and DISTRICT 6 (Chợ Lớn west) deepening. Chinese-Vietnamese (Hoa/Teochew) + canal heritage. Namespaced SEPARATE from SOURCES_HCMC.json / _CENTRAL / _OUTER / _CHOLON2 / etc.

outlets.name: VnExpress (Du lịch / Ngôi Sao)
outlets.note: Vietnam's largest online newspaper. Food-heritage reporting on District 8's hủ tiếu hồ shop and the Bến Bình Đông wharf; Ngôi Sao edition on Chùa An Phú and AEON Mall Bình Tân.

outlets.name: Thanh Niên
outlets.note: Major national daily. Features on the Teochew hủ tiếu hồ (Q8), the 180-year miểng-sành pagoda, District 6's most-famous chè shop, the Lê Quang Sung bánh hẹ stall, the 2026 Bến Bình Đông Tết flower market, and Chùa Huệ Nghiêm as Bình Tân's signature sight.

outlets.name: Tuổi Trẻ
outlets.note: Major Ho Chi Minh City daily; 'Lạc giữa thiên đường chè người Hoa - Chợ Lớn' feature on the Hoa dessert quarter.

outlets.name: Saigoneer
outlets.note: Leading English-language Saigon culture/street-food outlet; 'Hẻm Gems' feature on the Bửu Đình (D6) suan la fen stall (published in EN and VN).

outlets.name: Báo Phụ Nữ TP.HCM (Phụ Nữ Online)
outlets.note: Official Ho Chi Minh City Women's Union daily; corroborating feature on the Macao-style bún chua cay in Chợ Lớn.

outlets.name: Znews (formerly Zing News)
outlets.note: Established national news/lifestyle outlet; feature on beloved snack stalls of the Hoa quarter (corroborates the Lê Quang Sung bánh hẹ).

outlets.name: Người Đô Thị
outlets.note: Credible urban-affairs magazine; feature on the 150-year Đình Bình Đông marooned on a Kênh Đôi islet.

outlets.name: Ashui.com
outlets.note: Established Vietnamese architecture & urbanism portal; heritage piece on Bến Bình Đông / Đình Bình Đông.

outlets.name: Kenh14
outlets.note: Major Vietnamese lifestyle/news outlet; feature on six historic Saigon bridges including Cầu Nhị Thiên Đường / Cầu Chữ Y.

outlets.name: CafeBiz
outlets.note: Established business/news outlet (VCCorp); history of the Chinese-Vietnamese magnate behind Cầu Nhị Thiên Đường, 'the first cement bridge in Indochina'.

outlets.name: Báo Đầu Tư (Vietnam Investment Review)
outlets.note: Ministry of Planning & Investment newspaper; report on the opening of AEON Mall Bình Tân.

outlets.name: Wikipedia (Vietnamese)
outlets.note: Full articles used as lone institutional authority for sights: Chợ đầu mối Bình Điền, Chùa Huệ Nghiêm, Xóm Củi.

outlets.name: Pháp Luật TP.HCM
outlets.note: Major Ho Chi Minh City daily; feature on the origins of the Xóm Củi / Hưng Phú / Rạch Ông place-names in District 8.
